## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Esoteric sūtra-manual preserved only in the Manji Xùzàngjīng (X02 no. 204), attributed to **Amoghavajra** ([不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA)). The text presents the **Lotus-Sūtra samādhi** as an Esoteric *samaya* (sacred-vow / sacred-bond) — i.e. recasts the Lotus-sūtra meditation tradition within the Tang-period Esoteric *yoga-tantra* framework of *samaya*-vows linking practitioner to *kula* (Buddha-family).

**Abstract**

Amoghavajra produced a substantial corpus of texts integrating the *Lotus-sūtra* tradition with Esoteric ritual; his most influential such work is the *Dàlè jīngāng bùkōng zhēnshí sānmóyē jīng* ([KR6c0120](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0120) T243), the *Adhyardhaśatikā Prajñāpāramitā* in Tantric guise. The present *Miàofǎ liánhuá sānmèi mìmì sānmóyē jīng* extends that programme to the *Lotus*-tradition proper. Like [KR6j0226](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0226) it is preserved only via the Xùzàngjīng supplementary line; the authenticity of the Amoghavajra attribution is therefore uncertain. The text presupposes a developed *yoga-tantra* ritual framework and reads as a late-eighth-century or later production within Amoghavajra's school. The Japanese Tendai and Shingon traditions both draw on this text in their respective Lotus-meditation practices.
